To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Bayesian model selection (hierarchical) approach is more robust and informative than the Bayesian model selection approach and the frequentist approach.
the Bayesian hierarchical approach to model comparison is more robust than both the GBFs and classical frequentist tests of model evidences.
the GBF, a frequentist approach and a new Bayesian method for BMS at group level are compared.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to combine the results of BMS from several subjects.
how to combine the results of model selection across subjects.
the question of how to combine BMS results from multiple subjects in order to determine the most likely model across subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bayesian model selection is the best approach for group studies.
the new method is more robust and provides more information than the existing methods.
the new method proposed here, the hierarchical Bayesian model space, is the best way to combine results of BMS from multiple subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for group studies which is robust to outliers and provides a probability density over the models considered.

the hierarchical Bayesian method is a powerful and flexible approach for combining results across subjects and models, and that the method can be applied to any problem in which the data for each subject can be described by one or more competing hypotheses.
the new method provides a more robust approach to Bayesian model selection for group-level studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the random effects approach to BMS is a more powerful tool for group studies than the GBF, and is particularly well-suited for the analysis of large datasets, e.g. those generated by the Human Connectome Project.
it is crucial to take into account the heterogeneity of data between subjects and to account for the fact that the log-evidenced are not independent and identically distributed.
it is important to consider the full probability distribution of models when combining BMS results across subjects.
